plain_description.what: Removes question difficulty and general model ability with an item-response model, on 5,907 evaluation items x 18 models from a content-closed multi-source pool. It then measures how well the discovered cells explain which model does better. This is compared with random cells of the same sizes inside each source, and with per-source k-means clusters of matched count. No calls.
plain_description.why: Asks whether the discovered cells carry real which-model-wins information beyond the dataset source, and whether they beat a simple clustering baseline.
plain_description.information: Beating random cells means cells carry signal beyond source. Beating k-means would favour the discovered tree. Result: done. The cells beat random cells of the same size inside each source (explained share 0.053 vs 0.038 at the 97.5th percentile). But per-source k-means is slightly better than the tree as built, and that holds descriptively on own-source items too. This is not a routing gain and is tied to these 18 models.
